prompt: Why aren’t the Herculaneum scrolls simply unrolled?

options.text: They are carbonised and fall apart when handled
The law forbids anyone to touch them
They are glued shut with Roman resin

explanation: The scrolls turned to charcoal in the eruption; 18th-century attempts to open them destroyed many.

prompt: What was the first word read inside an unopened scroll, in 2023?
explanation: A 21-year-old student found porphyras, a rare Greek word meaning “purple”.

prompt: What does machine learning do in this work?

options.text: It finds the ink, which barely shows in the CT scans
It translates the Greek into English
It glues the scroll fragments back together

explanation: Carbon ink barely appears in the images; the models learn to recognise its traces.
misconception: The AI doesn’t “guess” the text: it locates the ink, and papyrologists read and check the letters.
